questions.q: A monochromatic light of frequency $5 \times 10^{14} \mathrm{~Hz}$ travelling through air, is incident on a medium of refractive index ' 2 '. Wavelength of the refracted light will be :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{f} \lambda=\mathrm{v} \quad \lambda_{\text {medium }}=\frac{\lambda_{\text {vacuum }}}{\mu}$
$\lambda_{\text {medium }} \Rightarrow \frac{3 \times 10^8}{2 \times 5 \times 10^{14}} \Rightarrow 0.3 \times 10^{-6} \Rightarrow 300 \mathrm{~nm}$

questions.q: In a Young's double-slit experiment, the ratio of the slit's width is $4: 1$ . The ratio of the intensity of maxima to minima, close to the central fringe on the screen, will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$Intensity∝widthofslit$
$\dfrac{{I}_{1}}{{I}_{2}} = \dfrac{4}{1}$.
$\dfrac{{I}_\max}{{I}_\min} = {\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{{I}_{1}} + \sqrt{{I}_{2}}}{\sqrt{{I}_{1}} - \sqrt{{I}_{2}}}\right)}^{2} = {\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{\dfrac{{I}_{1}}{{I}_{2}}} + 1}{\sqrt{\dfrac{{I}_{1}}{{I}_{2}}} - 1}\right)}^{2}$
$= {\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{4} + 1}{\sqrt{4} - 1}\right)}^{2} = {\left(\dfrac{3}{1}\right)}^{2} = \dfrac{9}{1}$
${I}_\max: {I}_\min = 9: 1$

questions.q: A monochromatic light of wavelength $6000\overset{o}{A}$ is incident on the single slit of width $0 . 01mm$. If the diffraction pattern is formed at the focus of the convex lens of focal length $20$ cm, the linear width of the central maximum is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The linear width of central maxima is given by,

$W = \dfrac{2\lambdaD}{d} = \dfrac{2 \times 6 \times {10}^{- 7} \times 0 .2}{1 \times {10}^{- 5}}$

$= 2 .4 \times {10}^{- 2} = 24mm$

questions.q: Two polaroids& $A\text{and}B$~are placed in such a way that the pass-axis of polaroids are perpendicular to each other. Now, another polaroid $C$ is placed between $A\text{and}B$ bisecting angle between them. If intensity of unpolarised light is ${I}_{0}$ then intensity of transmitted light after passing through polaroid~$B$ will be :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
As given here, the pass axis of polaroids& $A$ and $B$ are inclined at angle of ~$90 º$ with~each other. Another polaroid $C$is placed at angle of $45 °$with~respect to $A$~and~$B$.~

Therefore, intensity of light after falling on polaroid~$A, {I}_{A} = \dfrac{I0}{2}$

Intensity of light after falling on polaroid~$C, {I}_{C} = {I}_{A}\cos^{2}45 ° = \dfrac{I0}{2}\cos^{2}45 ° = \dfrac{I0}{4}$

Intensity of light after falling on~polaroid~$B, {I}_{B} = {I}_{C}\cos^{2}45 ° = \dfrac{I0}{4}\cos^{2}45 ° = \dfrac{I0}{8}$

questions.q: Using Young's double slit experiment, a monochromatic light of wavelength $5000 Å$ produces fringes of fringe width $0 . 5mm$. If another monochromatic light of wavelength $6000 Å$ is used and the separation between the slits is doubled, then the new fringe width will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
We know that fringe width is given by,& $\beta = \dfrac{\lambdaD}{d}$

$⇒ \dfrac{\beta '}{β} = \dfrac{\lambda '}{λ} \times \dfrac{d}{d '} = \dfrac{6000}{5000} \times \dfrac{d}{2d}$

$⇒ {β}^{'} = \dfrac{6}{5 \times 2} \times 0 . 5= 0 . 3mm$

questions.q: A light wave is propagating with plane wave fronts of the type $x+y+z=$ constant. The angle made by the direction of wave propagation with the $x$-axis is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The direction of propagation of light is perpendicular to the wave front and is symmetric about $\mathrm{x}, \mathrm{y}$ and z axis.
$\therefore$ Angle made by the light with $\mathrm{x}, \mathrm{y} \ \text{ and } \mathrm{z}$ axis is same.
$\therefore \quad \cos \alpha=\cos \beta=\cos \gamma(\alpha, \beta \ \text{ and } \gamma$ are angle made by light with $\mathrm{x}, \mathrm{y} \ \text{ and } \mathrm{z}$ axis respectively)
Also $\cos ^2 \alpha+\cos ^2 \beta+\cos ^2 \gamma=1$ [Sum of direction cosines]
$\therefore \alpha=\cos ^{-1} \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$

questions.q: A beam of unpolarised light of intensity ${I}_{0}$ is passed through a polaroid $A$ and then through another polaroid $B$ which is oriented so that its principal plane makes an angle of $45 °$ relative to that of $A$. The intensity of emergent light is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Intensity of polarised light from polaroid $A$ will be $\dfrac{I0}{2}$. Therefore,

Intensity of emergent light
$= \dfrac{I0}{2}\cos^{2}45 ° = \dfrac{I0}{4}$

questions.q: The aperture diameter of a telescope is $5m$ . The separation between the moon and the earth is $4 \times {10}^{5}km$ . With light of wavelength of $5500Å$ , the minimum separation between objects on the surface of moon, so that they are just resolved, is close to:

questions.solution:
$\theta = 1.22\dfrac{\lambda}{a}$
Distance $= {O}_{1}{O}_{2} = d\theta$
$= 1.22\dfrac{\lambda}{a}d$
Distance $= {O}_{1}{O}_{2} = \dfrac{1.22 \times 5893 \times {10}^{- 10} \times 4 \times {10}^{8}}{5} \approx 57.5m$
$∴$ answer from options $= 60m$
(minimum distance)

questions.q: In Young's double slits experiment, the position of 5<sup>th</sup> bright fringe from the central maximum is $5$ cm. The distance between slits and screen is $1m$ and wavelength of used monochromatic light is $600$ nm. The separation between the slits is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given here,&

$D = 1m$,~$\lambda = 600 \times {10}^{- 9}m$~and~$n = 5$

Distance of nth bright fringe is given by, ${y}_{n} = \dfrac{n\lambdaD}{d}$, where,~$d$~is separation between the slits.

$⇒ \dfrac{5 \times 600 \times {10}^{- 9} \times 1}{d} = 5 \times {10}^{- 2}$

$⇒ d = \dfrac{5 \times 600 \times {10}^{- 9} \times 1}{5 \times {10}^{- 2}} = 60 \times {10}^{- 6}m$

$⇒ d = 60\mum$.

questions.q: The two light beams having intensities $I$~and $9I$ interfere to produce a fringe pattern on a screen. The phase difference between the beams is $\dfrac{π}{2}$~at point $P$ and $\pi$ at point $Q$. Then the difference between the resultant intensities at $P$ and $Q$ will be :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Resultant intensity is given by,& ${I}_{resultant} = {I}_{1} + {I}_{2} + 2\sqrt{{I}_{1}{I}_{2}}cosϕ$

At $P$,~${I}_{P} = 9I + I + 2\sqrt{9I \times I}cos\left(\dfrac{π}{2}\right) = 10I$

At~$Q$,~${I}_{Q} = 9I + I + 2\sqrt{9I \times I}cos\left(\pi\right) = 10I - 2 \times 3I = 4I$

Now, difference between intensities is~$10I - 4I = 6I$

questions.q: ‘$n$’ polarizing sheets are arranged such that each makes an angle $45 °$ with the proceeding sheet. An unpolarized light of intensity $I$ is incident into this arrangement. The output intensity is found to be $\dfrac{I}{64}$ . The value of $n$ will be:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
When an unpolarized light& passes& through a polariser, the intensity of the emergent light from the polariser depends on the square of the cosine of the angle between the plane of the polariser and the direction of the incident light.

The formula to calculate the intensity& \left({I}_{1}\right)$~of the emergent light from a polariser which makes an angle~$\theta$~with the direction of the incident light is given by

${I}_{1} = I\cos^{2}\theta . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ( 1 )$

where,~$I$~is the intensity of the incident light.

Substitute~$45 °$~for~$\theta$~into equation (1) to obtain the intensity of the first emergent light.

$\begin{cases}{I}_{1} & = & I\cos^{2}45 ° \\ & = & \dfrac{I}{2}\end{cases}$

In a similar manner, the intensity~ \left({I}_{2}\right)$~of the second emergent light can be written as

$\begin{cases}{I}_{2} & = & {I}_{1}\cos^{2}45 ° \\ & = & \dfrac{I1}{2} \\ & = & \dfrac{I}{4} \\ & = & \dfrac{I}{22}\end{cases}$

Thus, for~$n$~number of such polarisers, the net intensity~ \left({I}_{n}\right)$~of the emergent light can be written as

${I}_{n} = \dfrac{I}{2n} . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ( 1 )$

Comparing equation (1) with the given expression for the intensity, it can be concluded that

$n = 6$

$

questions.q:
Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion-(A) : If Young's double slit experiment is performed in an optically denser medium than air, then the consecutive fringes come closer.
Reason-(R) : The speed of light reduces in an optically denser medium than air while its frequency does not change.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both $(\mathbf{A})$ and $(\mathbf{R})$ are true but $(\mathbf{R})$ is not the correct explanation of $(\mathbf{A})$
Both $(\mathbf{A})$ and $(\mathbf{R})$ are true and $(\mathbf{R})$ is the correct explanation of $(\mathbf{A})$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\beta(\text { fringe width })=\frac{\lambda D}{d}$ In denser medium, $\lambda \downarrow \Rightarrow \beta \downarrow\Rightarrow$ fringe come closer Also, $\mu=\frac{\mathrm{c}}{\mathrm{V}} \Rightarrow \mathrm{V}=\frac{\mathrm{c}}{\mu}$
Frequency remains same,
$\Rightarrow \mu=\frac{\lambda_{\mathrm{vac} .} \mathrm{f}}{\lambda_{\mathrm{med}} \mathrm{f}} \Rightarrow \lambda_{\mathrm{med}}=\frac{\lambda_{\mathrm{vac} .}}{\mu}$

questions.q: A polarizer - analyser set is adjusted such that the intensity of light coming out of the analyser is just $36%$ of the original intensity. Assuming that the polarizer - analyser set does not absorb any light, the angle by which the analyser needs to be rotated further, to reduce the output intensity to zero, is~  \left(\sin^{- 1} \left(\dfrac{3}{5}\right) =37 °\right)$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$I = {I}_{0}cos^{2}\theta$
$0 . 36{I}_{0} = {I}_{0}\cos^{2}\theta$
$cos\left(\theta\right) = \dfrac{3}{5}$

$⇒ \theta = 53 °$
~
angle rotated should be $= {90}^{o} - {53}^{o} = {37}^{o}$

questions.q: Two coherent light sources having intensity in the ratio $2x$~produce an interference pattern. The ratio $\dfrac{{I}_\max - {I}_\min}{{I}_\max + {I}_\min}$ will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given that, $\dfrac{I1}{I2} = 2x$.

We know,

${I}_\max = \left(\sqrt{{I}_{1}} + \sqrt{{I}_{2}}\right)2 \text{ and } {I}_\min = \left(\sqrt{{I}_{1}} - \sqrt{{I}_{2}}\right)2$

$∴ \dfrac{{I}_\max - {I}_\min}{{I}_\max + {I}_\min} = \dfrac{2\sqrt{{I}_{1}{I}_{2}}}{{I}_{1} + {I}_{2}} = \dfrac{2\sqrt{{I}_{1} / {I}_{2}}}{\dfrac{I1}{I2} + 1} = \dfrac{2\sqrt{2x}}{2x + 1}$

questions.q: In a double slit experiment, when a thin film of thickness $t$ having refractive index $\mu$ is introuduced in front of one of the slits, the maximum at the centre of the fringe pattern shifts by one fringe width. The value of $t$ is $( \lambda$ is the wavelength of the light used):
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Shift $= \left(\mu - 1\right)t\dfrac{D}{d}$
Fringe width $( \beta ) = \dfrac{\lambdaD}{d}$
$( \mu - 1 ) t\dfrac{D}{d} = \lambda\dfrac{D}{d}$
$t = \dfrac{\lambda}{\mu - 1}$

questions.q: Two beams of light having intensities $I$~and $4I$ interfere to produce a fringe pattern on a screen. The phase difference between the two beams are $\dfrac{π}{2}$~and $\dfrac{π}{3}$~at points $A$ and $B$ respectively. The difference between the resultant intensities at the two points is $xI$. The value of $x$ will be _____ .
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given here, phase difference at point& $A$~and~$B$~are~${ϕ}_{A} = \dfrac{π}{2}$and~${ϕ}_{B} = \dfrac{π}{3}$.

Resultant intensity at point~$A$,~

${I}_{A} = I + 4I + 2\sqrt{I}\sqrt{4I}cos \left(\dfrac{π}{2}\right)

$⇒ {I}_{A} = 5I + 4I\left($0\right) = 5I$

Resultant intensity at point~$B$,

${I}_{B} = I + 4I + 2$\sqrt{I}\sqrt{4I}$cos \left(60 °\right)$~$= 5I + 4I \times \dfrac{1}{2} = 7I$

Difference in intensities is~${I}_{B} - {I}_{A} = 7I - 5I = 2I$.

Thus, value of~$x = 2.

$

questions.q: In a Young's double slit experiment, the slits are separated by $0 . 3mm$ and the screen is $1 . 5m$ away from the plane of slits. Distance between fourth bright fringes on both sides of central bright fringe is $2 . 4cm .$ The frequency of light used is $x \times {10}^{14}Hz .$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The distance between $n^{th}$ bright fringe on both side of central maxima is $2 . 4cm .$~The $f = ?$

$\Deltay = \dfrac{D\lambda}{d} \times 8$
$\lambda = \dfrac{d\Deltay}{8D} = \dfrac{0 . 3 \times {10}^{- 3} \times 2 . 4 \times {10}^{- 2}}{8 \times 1 . 5} = \dfrac{0 . 12 \times {10}^{- 5}}{2} = 0 . 06 \times {10}^{- 5}$
$\lambda = 6 \times {10}^{- 7}m$
$f = \dfrac{C}{6 \times {10}^{- 7}} = 0 . 5 \times {10}^{+ 15}$
$f = 5 \times {10}^{14}Hz$
So, $x = 5$

questions.q: A parallel beam of monochromatic light of wavelength $600 \mathrm{~nm}$ passes through single slit of $0.4 \mathrm{~mm}$ width. Angular divergence corresponding to second order minima would be ______ $\times 10^{-3} \mathrm{rad}$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\sin \theta \simeq \theta \simeq \frac{2 \lambda}{b}=\frac{2 \times 600 \times 10^{-9}}{4 \times 10^{-4}}=3 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{rad}$
Total divergence $=(3+3) \times 10^{-3}=6 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{rad}$

questions.q: As shown in figures, three identical polaroids ${P}_{1}$, ${P}_{2}$ and ${P}_{3}$ are placed one after another. The pass axis of ${P}_{2}$ and ${P}_{3}$ are inclined at angle of $60 º$ and $90 º$ with respect to axis of ${P}_{1}$. The source $S$ has an intensity of~$256Wm^{- 2}$.~The intensity of light at point $O$ is _____Wm^{- 2}.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
As given here, the pass axis of ${P}_{2}$ and ${P}_{3}$ are inclined at angle of $60 º$ and $90 º$ with respect to axis of ${P}_{1}$.~

Therefore, intensity of light after falling on first polaroid~${P}_{1}, {I}_{1} = \dfrac{I0}{2}$

Intensity of light after falling on second~polaroid~${P}_{2}, {I}_{2} = {I}_{1}\cos^{2}60 ° = \dfrac{I0}{8}$

Intensity of light after falling on third~polaroid~${P}_{3}, {I}_{3} = {I}_{2}\cos^{2}30 ° = \dfrac{I0}{8}\left(\dfrac{3}{4}\right) = \dfrac{3{I}_{0}}{32}$

The intensity of light at~$O$~is~$\dfrac{3{I}_{0}}{32} = \dfrac{3 \times 256}{32} = 24Wm^{- 2}$
